Only 17 of 50 US states have a capital that is also their largest city. A thread on the capitals that lost out to a bigger neighbour.

a thread 🧵🗺️

1/ In 33 states the biggest city is somewhere else: Texas (Houston, not Austin), California (Los Angeles, not Sacramento), Florida (Jacksonville), New York (New York City), Pennsylvania (Philadelphia), Illinois (Chicago). Data: Wikipedia, US 2020 Census.
2/ Some gaps are stark. Montana: Billings is larger than Helena. Nevada: Las Vegas outgrew Carson City. Washington: Seattle, not Olympia. Washington, DC is a city, not a state, so it isn't shown.
3/ Canada is closer to even: 8 of 13 provinces and territories have a capital that is also the largest city, including Ontario (Toronto), Manitoba (Winnipeg) and Nova Scotia (Halifax).

4/ The exceptions are Quebec (Montreal is larger than Quebec City) and BC (Vancouver is larger than Victoria). The tally: 25 matches, 38 non-matches across the 63 states, provinces and territories shown.

Cities are counted by city proper, not metro area, so a different definition could change some answers. Which capital that isn't the biggest city surprises you most? Follow @forummapping for more maps like this.
